messages:
maria: Noticed a regression after the multi-variant routing change. Batch sizes for mixed-compat requests dropped ~30% and KV cache miss rate spiked. Attaching a short perf snippet from the profiler. cc @kevin @jess :eyes:

kevin: Ugh. Is this only on the compat-fallback path or also on normal same-variant traffic? Any recent kernel selector changes?

maria: Only mixed-variant (compat set) traffic. Same-variant throughput looks fine. We changed the routing to prefer lower-latency variants first and enable cross-variant fallbacks. Kernel selector hasn't changed in the last deploy.

sam: Could be queue shape + token budget interaction. If routing admits small quick variants first they can consume slots and fragment the batch window. Do you have queue wait histograms?

maria: Pasted small dumps:
```
queue_wait_ms p50: 8 p95: 120 p99: 430
batch_size mean: 6 -> 4 (mixed traffic)
kv_cache_hit: 0.74 -> 0.58
```
Looks correlated with p95 tail.

jess: Also check the compat set grouping key. Right now we only compare by dtype/seq_len bucket, but kernel compatibility requires contiguous weight layout too. We might be over-constraining compat sets so fallback routing ends up selecting a variant incompatible with fast kernels, forcing slower kernel + smaller micro-batches.

kevin: Good point. If the kernel selection falls back to a generic CUDA kernel we lose the fused attention paths and throughput collapses. Any traces showing kernel name choices?

maria: From profiler: most mixed batches ended up on kernel 'attn_generic_v2' instead of 'attn_fused_4bit'.

sam: That explains it. Two levers I think: 1) relax routing ordering so that compatible variants get grouped and scheduled together (even if slightly higher latency), 2) adjust token_budget_target upward for mixed compat queues so scheduler holds for slightly larger coalescing windows.

jess: I worry about increasing token_budget globally — could regress strict latency SLOs for tiny interactive requests. We should scope it per-compat-set and fallback-tier. Maybe add an override: if incoming variant set intersects fast-kernel family, set token_budget_target = default * 1.5 only for that batch pool.

kevin: Agree. Also consider heuristic: allow ephemeral kernel recompile hints that accept minor layout transformations to avoid generic fallback (cheap transpose path). Could be a stopgap while we improve kernel selector.

maria: Proposed experiment: for next canary, 1) increase compat coalescing window for cross-variant queues from 8ms -> 14ms, 2) add per-compat-set token_budget multiplier 1.4, 3) log chosen kernel name into metric with tag variant_set. Roll for 2 hours and compare batch_size, kv_hit, and p95.

sam: 👍 start with a single node of heavy mixed workload. We'll need a flag so we can revert quickly. I can wire up the metrics dashboard to show kernel_name and batch_size over time.

runtime-bot: Deploy plan created: canary/group=eng-runtime-mix1 node=rt-mix-03 window_ms=14 token_mult=1.4 -> scheduled at 2026-03-18T09:30:00Z.

maria: Added a quick patch to the routing config:
```
compat_coalesce_ms: 14
token_budget_multiplier_by_compat:
  fast-kernel-family: 1.4
  default: 1.0
log_kernel_name: true
```
Patch link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/changes/1982

kevin: If that stabilizes batch sizes and we see kernel_name flip back to fused ones, we can iterate on making kernel selector prefer fused-compatible variants at routing time instead of as a post-hoc heuristic.

jess: Also add a small kv-cache warmup for fallback targets — when routing decides to include a fallback variant, prefetch prefix KV entries for it in the background. Might reduce the kv miss spike. Low-risk small async task.

maria: Good idea. I'll add prefetch logic as opt-in for the canary.

sam: I'll set up the dashboard + alert: if batch_size drops >15% OR kv_hit drops >8% revert canary automatically.

maria: Thanks team. Action items: sam -> dashboard/alerts, jess -> prefetch patch, kevin -> kernel selector follow-ups, me -> deploy & observe. Will report back after 2 hours. :rocket:

kevin: :thumbsup:
